Rule 1 changes from "the transaction is valid, may be included in a block and aborts exceptionally" to "the transaction is invalid"; rule 2 states the initcode cost is part of the intrinsic gas cost; rule 3 changes CREATE and CREATE2 oversize behaviour from exceptional abort to pushing 0 on the stack; the "How to report initcode limit violation?" rationale is rewritten accordingly; two test cases about intrinsic-gas coverage are added; Andrei Maiboroda is added as an author.

inclusions.normalization_rationale: On ACD(E) 153 (2023-01-19) the moderator proposed including the EIP-6049 deprecation announcement in Shanghai; after discussion and no disagreement he concluded it is "still included" and that he would edit the Shanghai spec. The execution-specs commit authored the same day ("Add EIP-6049", merged via PR #689, body "Decided in ACDE#153", on 2023-01-23) added it directly to the "Included EIPs" section with the no-behavior-change note. EIP-6049 never passed through the CFI stage - as a Meta deprecation notice it required no devnet testing - so the single event normalizes to included. occurred_at uses the decision/commit-author date; the PR merged four days later.
inclusions.raw_label: Added directly to "Included EIPs" as a deprecation announcement ("Decided in ACDE#153"; "the two places ... I would edit is like the Shanghai spec ... and any announcement we make of the upgrade")

revisions.rationale: Recorded as substantive because the Standards Track/Core to Meta reclassification changes the document's normative standing in the EIP process - it is the field that tells client teams whether the proposal is a protocol change requiring implementation. This is the classification the Shanghai fork record later relies on when distinguishing EIP-6049 from the fork's core protocol changes. change_type is clarification rather than normative_behavior because no specification text was altered; the change makes explicit what the creation text already implied ('No changes to clients is applicable'). Confidence is medium: a narrower reading would treat a frontmatter-only edit as editorial metadata. The merging pull request (#6064) carries only the repository's PR-template boilerplate, so no author rationale is on record (gh-pr-6064).

notes: The window begins before creation of the Shanghai upgrade document and includes the full mainnet activation sequence.
Numbered withdrawal devnets retain their first attributable genesis; later resets are preserved in notes rather than replacing the initial launch marker.
During Shapella planning, "Scheduled for Inclusion" had not yet been formalized. Pre-activation commitments were labeled "Included"; under the later EIP-7723 vocabulary, these are SFI-equivalent.

unknowns: EIP-6049 is a no-behavior-change deprecation announcement. It appears on Shapella activation milestones, where it was part of the canonical fork, but is intentionally not assigned developer-network participation unsupported by a protocol transition.
Capella includes consensus-layer changes that have no EIP numbers. Task 01 inventories only the cross-layer EIP-4895, so no consensus-only EIP lanes are invented.
The archived withdrawal network repository contains many rapid relaunches. This timeline applies the task-wide earliest-attributable-launch rule and does not add a separate marker for every reset.
